items.headline: Tourism Heads to COP31 Wanting Results, Not More Pledges
items.body: Five years after the Glasgow Declaration, tourism has plenty of climate commitments but little shared proof of what they’ve achieved. The industry is still split on whether better measurement or faster action should come first.

items.headline: Qatar’s Tourism Recovery is Coming by Road, Not Air
items.body: Qatar’s visitor numbers are recovering on road traffic across the Saudi border, while air arrivals keep falling. Drive-in visitors tend to make shorter trips, which limits how much they can do for hotels.

items.headline: Bomb Hoaxes Test Europe’s Airlines as Geopolitical Pressures Mount
items.body: None of this week’s threats has proved real, but each one still cost a diversion, a search and a rebuilt schedule. Whoever sent them, the hoaxes have added to a list of disruptions, from conflict-driven fuel costs to closed airspace, that is making routine flying in Europe ever more challenging.

items.headline: Airbnb-Backed Candidates Lose in LA, a Setback in Push to Loosen Rental Rules
items.body: Airbnb’s money may not have bought it a friendlier mayor in Los Angeles. Expect the company to look for other ways to add Olympic supply.

items.headline: Airbnb Outpaces Rivals With Its Fastest Revenue Growth in 3 Years

items.headline: Airbnb CEO: Our Specialized AI Agents Will Handle ‘Every Vertical in Travel’
items.body: There's been speculation for years about whether Airbnb would launch flights. Such small-minded speculation: Airbnb intends to use specialized AI agents to do every travel vertical. Airbnb Cruise, anyone?
